cleaningTypes.guideIntro: Sweepr jobs come in four cleaning types. Here is what each one involves, in plain language, so you know exactly what you are signing up for.
cleaningTypes.acceptSubtitle: Choose which kinds of jobs Sweepr may offer you. You can change this anytime in Settings. At least one type is required.
cleaningTypes.atLeastOne: You must accept at least one job type.
cleaningTypes.deepNote: Deep Cleans are part of Standard jobs: when a home needs significantly more attention, the job carries a higher workload and pays accordingly, but it stays in the Standard category.

standard.title: Standard
standard.body: The everyday clean for lived-in homes: bathrooms, kitchen counters, bedrooms, living areas, vacuuming, and mopping. Most Sweepr jobs are Standard cleans.

deep.title: Deep Clean
deep.body: A Standard job that is automatically classified as a Deep Clean when the home needs significantly more attention (heavier buildup, longer time between cleanings). Expect a noticeably higher workload; the job is priced accordingly and your pay reflects the extra work. You do not opt into Deep Cleans separately: they arrive as Standard jobs with the Deep Clean label.

moveInOut.title: Move-In / Move-Out
moveInOut.body: A deep-level service for an empty home between occupants, including inside cabinets, drawers, closets, and shelving. The scope is strict: cleaning only. Moving belongings, organizing, packing, or hauling items is never part of the job. If a home is not actually empty, report it rather than working around it.

airbnb.title: Airbnb / Turnover
airbnb.body: A short-term rental turnover on a fixed time window between checkout and the next check-in. Bed-making with fresh linens, loading the dishwasher, and a basic patio sweep are included in the base scope. Window discipline is strict: the property must be guest-ready before the window closes, so plan the work to finish on time, every time.
